newsitem.title: UK: Copper prices face further declines in 1997 - Man.
newsitem.headline: Copper prices face further declines in 1997 - Man.

text.p: Copper prices will rebound from the lows by year end and remain firmer going into 1997 only to weaken later in the year as more mined production hits the market, said Fred Demler, minerals economist at E D and F Man International in a report released during LME Week.

Demler forecast copper prices will bottom out at 83 to 86 cents and rebound to 95 to 100 cents by year end. In 1997 prices will firm initially then ease as more production comes on stream. Prices in 1997 will range from 110 to 75 cents per pound.
Production will rise from 2.53 million tons in the fourth quarter of this year to 2.7 million in the final quarter of next year.

Consumption will rise from 2.63 million tons in the fourth quarter of this year to a peak of 2.82 million in the second quarter of next year before slipping to 2.69 million tons in the final quarter of 1997.
Supply, which includes East/West trade, will rise from 2.64 million tons in the fourth quarter of this year to 2.8 million tons in the final quarter of next year.
Stocks will rise as supply outstrips consumption, rising from 5.6 weeks of consumption in the final quarter of this year to 6.1 weeks in the comparable period next year.
Demler expected a market surplus of 25,000 tonnes in the fourth quarter, with deficits in the first and second quarters of next year, and surpluses in the final two quarters.

Delta hedging, which accelerated the steep falls in copper prices earlier this year, will be less of a problem as producers sell put options. Sumitomo's long position is "largely covered", Demler said.
There may be a "lower spot price without Hamanaka support," Demler suggested, referring to Sumitomo's fallen star copper trader, Yasuo Hamanaka.
